scope: concurrent rotate() calls from two browser tabs with same refresh token — precise await-interleaving analysis

evidence.observation: Full rotate() body. The last synchronous statement before the first await is repo.revoke(row.id) at line 60. The first await is users.findById() at line 61.
repo.revoke(row.id) is the LAST synchronous write before the first await. After this line executes, the token row has revoked_at set in the DB and Tab A yields the event loop.
revoke() is synchronous (better-sqlite3 .run() is blocking). The UPDATE is committed before revoke() returns. Tab A sees this write before yielding.
Tab B reads the row after Tab A's revoke() has committed. row.revoked_at is now non-null. Tab B enters this branch, calls revokeFamily() synchronously, and throws TokenReuseDetected.

revokeFamily() is fully synchronous. Both UPDATEs complete before revokeFamily() returns. Because Node.js is single-threaded and Tab B's code path (L52-throw) has no await, Tab B's entire revokeFamily() executes to completion BEFORE Tab A can resume from its await.

Tab A's repo.insert() always runs AFTER Tab B's revokeFamily() has already committed both UPDATEs — this ordering is deterministic because Tab B's path is entirely synchronous while Tab A is suspended at an await.
When TokenReuseDetected is thrown by Tab B, refreshController clears the rt cookie and sends 401. Tab B's browser loses its rt cookie.
Tab A's rotate() returns { access, refresh }. The new rt cookie is set and a new access token is issued. But the new token's fid (family_id) is the same family that Tab B just revoked.

hypotheses.statement: repo.revoke(row.id) at L60 is the last synchronous statement before the first await (users.findById at L61). After L60 commits, the row has revoked_at set and Tab A yields.
Tab B's entire execution from L52 to the thrown TokenReuseDetected is synchronous (no await). It runs to completion — including revokeFamily() — while Tab A is suspended at its await.
Tab A's repo.insert() at L64 always executes AFTER Tab B's revokeFamily() has committed both UPDATEs. This ordering is deterministic, not probabilistic.

Tab A inserts a new refresh token (revoked_at=NULL) into a family that is already marked revoked. The new token escapes the revokeFamily UPDATE because it did not exist yet when that UPDATE ran. Tab A then returns a new access token whose fid points to a revoked family.
Tab A's new access token is immediately rejected by authMiddleware on the next request because isFamilyRevoked(fid) returns true (family was revoked by Tab B). Both tabs end up logged out.
